title: Software Development & IT Consultants

rows.before: <li>We prepare the SR&ED claim on Form T661 alongside your software development corporation T2 return for qualifying experimental development work \u2014 the 35% refundable ITC on the first $3 million in eligible expenditures can recover a significant portion of your developer salaries, cloud compute for R&D environments, and subcontractor coding fees each fiscal year.<\/li>\r\n

rows.section: Services grid - tax planning card bullet
rows.before: <li>We plan SR&ED claims within CRA's 18-month filing deadline and coordinate the timing with your software corporation's fiscal year-end to maximize the refundable ITC \u2014 for CCPCs with taxable capital under $10 million, the 35% refundable rate applies to the first $3 million in qualifying expenditures, and we ensure your claim captures all eligible developer time, experimental cloud compute, and subcontractor coding costs.<\/li>\r\n
We prioritize catch-up T2 returns where the 18-month window has not yet closed to recover those credits before the deadline passes.
rows.note: SR&ED deadline fact stays; offer to recover SR&ED credits dropped

rows.before: <li>We correct misclassified SR&ED expenditures where your previous accountant lumped qualifying experimental development labour with general operating expenses on prior T2 returns \u2014 properly separating eligible costs and filing amended Form T661 claims recovers SR&ED refunds that were never claimed for each affected fiscal year within the 18-month deadline.<\/li>\r\n

rows.section: Services grid - CRA audit card bullet
rows.before: <li>We defend SR&ED claims during a CRA audit on your software development corporation by presenting Form T661 project descriptions, developer time-tracking records, Git commit history, Jira sprint documentation, and evidence of technological uncertainty \u2014 CRA denies SR&ED when no contemporaneous records support the qualifying experimental development work claimed.<\/li>\r\n
